title: Haile Selassie
summary: Haile Selassie, born Tafari Makonnen, ruled Ethiopia as regent and then emperor, crowned on 2 November 1930. He went into exile in 1936 after the Italian invasion, returned in 1941 with British help, and was deposed by the Derg in September 1974; he died in August 1975.

uncertainty.note: Birth date agrees across two opened pages; the death day 27 August 1975 appears on one page, the other gives only August 1975.

as_recorded.value: Crowned Emperor November 2, 1930; exile May 2, 1936; return to Addis Ababa May 5, 1941; deposed September 12, 1974

where.modern_name: Ejersa Goro, eastern Ethiopia (birthplace; later life centred on Addis Ababa)
where.historical_name: Ejersa Goro (Ejersa Gora / Ejarsa Gora), Harar province, Ethiopian Empire

importance.justification: Last emperor of Ethiopia, a symbol of resistance to the Italian occupation and a central figure in 20th-century African politics.

sources.title: Biography of Emperor Haile Selassie I

reviewer_note: Sources disagree on when his regency began (1916 vs 1917), so the summary only says regent. Biography.com lists Harar as birth city but its text names Ejersa Gora; the pin is the village. Both sources are non-scholarly; a scholarly biography should replace them at expansion.
